Starts a note on voice music_voice. A = pitch (0-$bf). Sets the frequency, effects, note time, filter sweep, pulse width and gate.
Pointer into the frequency table at $9edd (2 bytes for each pitch).
Loads the effect speed and the effect flags of the instrument.
Loads phase 0 of the effect steps of the voice.
Note time = note length of the voice.
Starts the filter sweep from its start cutoff.
Sets the pulse width of the instrument.
Clears the test bit and sets the gate.
The note uses 1 byte of data.
Does the command byte A of the music data. $c0-$cf set the note length. $f0-$f9 go through the handler table at $a0af.
Note length = entry (low nibble) of the duration table at $a05d.
Finds the command byte in the table at $a0a5. Y = 1 points to the argument.
No handler: the byte is not used.
No handler: bytes $d0-$ef and $fa-$ff. The read offset does not move, so music_tick reads the same byte again and does not end. No tune has such a byte.
Command $f0: rest. Waits for one note length without a new gate.
Stops the read of the voice for this tick.
Command $f1: sets the read offset of the voice to 0 and clears the gate. The tune starts again.
Command $f2: ends the tune of the voice. Stops the voice, its effects and the filter sweep.
Command $f3 n: loads instrument n, 12 bytes at $a3a6 + n * 12. Sets ADSR, waveform, pulse width and the effect steps.
Multiplies n by 12.
Byte 0: attack/decay. Byte 1: sustain/release.
Byte 2: waveform (high nibble) and pulse width high (low nibble).
Byte 3: pulse width low. The pulse width bytes are inverted.
Byte 4: effect speed. Byte 5: effect flags.
Bytes 6-11: value and length of the 3 effect phases.
Flag bit 1: sets the sync bit.
Flag bit 2: sets triangle with ring modulation ($14).
Command $f4 a b: note length = duration a + duration b (low nibbles, table at $a05d).
Command $f5 n: the voice continues with tune n from its start. Clears the filter routing bit of the voice.
Clears the resonance and the filter bit of the voice.
Command $f6 n: sets CIA 1 timer B (the music tick rate) to entry n of the tempo table at $a07d.
Command $f7 n: plays tune n on the voice, then returns after this command (see cmd_return).
Returns with X = music_voice * 2.
Command $f8: returns to the tune and read offset that cmd_call_tune saved.
Command $f9 n: loads filter setting n (11 bytes, pointer table at $a0c3) and starts the filter on this voice.
Byte 0: sweep speed. Bytes 1-2: start cutoff (high, low).
Byte 3: resonance and routing, with the bit of this voice.
Byte 4: filter mode. Clears the voice 3 off bit.
Bytes 5-10: step (times 8) and length of the 3 sweep phases.
Adds A to the read offset of voice music_voice. Returns X = music_voice * 2.
Decrements the note time of each voice. At 0, clears the gate. Also decrements the fade delay.
Clears the gate and the test bit of the voice.
Does one step of the effects of each voice: pitch steps, pulse sweep and frequency slide, in 3 phases.
Bit 7 clear: the effects of the voice are off.
Waits until the effect delay is 0.
Length 0, or all steps done: goes to the next phase.
Goes to the next of the 3 phases. After phase 2, loops only when flag bit 3 is set.
Flag bit 6: adds the step value to the pitch of voice X and sets the frequency from the table at $9edd.
Keeps the pitch below $c0.
Flag bit 5: adds the step value times 16 to the pulse width of voice X.
Flag bit 4: adds the step value to the frequency of voice X. Bit 7 of the phase length makes the step negative.
Does one step of the filter sweep: adds the step of the phase to the cutoff, in 3 phases.
Speed 0: no sweep.
After phase 2, the sweep starts again only when the step of phase 1 is not 0.
Adds the step of the filter phase to the 11-bit cutoff, then sets the cutoff.
Writes the 11-bit cutoff filter_cutoff to the SID shadow (low 3 bits, high 8 bits).
Starts the tune that sound_request,x asks for on voice X. When sound is off, drops requests of $83 and higher.
Stops the effects, the note time and the filter sweep. Read offset = 0.
Clears the resonance and the filter bit of the voice.
Fades the master volume in (to 15) or out (to 0), one step after each fade delay.
Silences the SID. Clears the SID shadow, the driver workspace $0200-$0259 and the driver variables $ce-$ed.
Silences the SID. Clears the SID shadow, the driver workspace $0200-$0259 and the driver variables $cf-$ee.
32 bytes: the last byte $ee is after freq_slide_step_hi, and nothing uses it.
Copies the SID shadow ($31-$49) to the SID registers $d400-$d418.
Effects tick on CIA 1 timer A. Updates the effects and the filter sweep, then writes the SID.
Does nothing while the music tick runs.
SID frequency of each quarter tone: 192 words, low byte first, 24 steps for each octave. Note byte n uses entry 2n. The driver adds the base $9edd as two immediates at $99b4 and $9d41.

SID frequencies, 192 words, low byte first. Entry 2n is the NTSC value of semitone n ($00-$5f). Each odd entry is the mean of its two neighbours, and the last entry is $ffff. Note byte n uses entry 2n. The tunes use the notes $01-$54. The driver adds the base $9edd as two immediates at $99b4 and $9d41.
Note lengths in music ticks, 16 words. Event bytes $c0-$cf select entry 0-15. Command $f4 adds two entries.
Note lengths in music ticks, 16 words. Event bytes $c0-$cf select entry 0-15. Command $f4 adds two entries. No tune uses the entries 12-15.
CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. A larger value gives a slower tune.

CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. Each value is 1000000 / (music ticks each second): 16 to 80 ticks each second at 1 MHz. A PAL C64 runs 1.5% slower. The tunes use only the entries $0a-$10.
Offset of the SID registers of voice 0, 1 and 2 (0, 7, 14) in the SID copy at $31.
Offset of voice 0, 1 and 2 in the effect phase tables at $0200 and $0209 (3 phases each).
The command bytes $f0-$f9 of the tune data. The driver compares an event byte with each entry.
Handler of each command $f0-$f9: rest, restart, end, instrument, length, goto, tempo, call, return, filter.
Pointers to the 16 filter settings of command $f9.
Pointers to the 16 filter settings of command $f9. No tune selects filter settings 0 and 9.
Filter setting, 11 bytes. Bytes 0-4: step delay, cutoff high, cutoff low, resonance and routing, mode. Then 3 phases: cutoff step (x 8), step count.
Start of each tune, 114 words (tunes $00-$71). The sound request $80+n in $dd-$df starts tune n.

Start of each tune, 114 words (tunes $00-$71). The sound request $80+n in $dd-$df starts tune n. No request and no tune selects tunes $58, $59, $60, $65-$68 and $6f-$71. Tunes $58, $59 and $65-$68 hold only $f2.
Tune data: bytes $00-$bf are notes, $c0-$cf select a note length, $f0-$f9 are commands with 0-2 argument bytes.

Instruments of command $f3, 12 bytes each (63 entries). Command $f3 n reads entry n at $a3a6+12n. Bytes 0-3: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform with inverted pulse width high, inverted pulse width low. Bytes 4-5: effect delay, effect flags. Then 3 phases: value, length.

Instruments of command $f3, 12 bytes each (63 entries). Command $f3 n reads entry n at $a3a6+12n. Bytes 0-3: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform with inverted pulse width high, inverted pulse width low. Bytes 4-5: effect delay, effect flags. Then 3 phases: value, length. No tune loads instruments $2f, $30, $36, $38 and $39.

Work bitmap of the fight area: 8 character rows of 320 bytes (bitmap rows 14-21). The fighters are drawn here. The arena change at $8e8d also uses $a69a-$b699 as 16 rows of 256 bytes and swaps it with $d000-$dfff.
Columns 4-35 of each work bitmap row start at $a6ba+320k (256 bytes). $8cc7 copies them to the screen bitmap.
Clean copy of the fight area: 8 character rows of 320 bytes (bitmap rows 14-21), $b09a-$ba99.
Columns 4-35 of bitmap row 14+k, at $b0ba+320k. $8c5b fills them, $8c91 copies them to the work bitmap.
Pointers to the 24 texts. The text printer at $92eb draws text $80+n from entry n.

Text format: column, row, colour byte, then characters. $0d starts a new line with 3 new header bytes. The colour byte goes to screen RAM (high nibble) and colour RAM (low nibble). Other characters than A-Z and text_special_chars end the text. Text 0: "000" at row 22. No code prints text 0.
Text 1: the version "V 05 10 87". A second line has "WHY DID YOU PRESS ME" at column 10, row 18. CTRL+V shows it. Build V 05 05 87 has no second line.
Texts 2-4: "1PLR", "2PLR" and "DEMO" at row 24.
Text 5: "PAUSED". No code prints text 5.
Text 6: two digits at row 5. $8297 writes the time ($c8) or the level ($be) into them.
Texts 7 and 8: the 5-digit scores of fighter 0 and 1 at row 5.
Text 9: "YOUR END HAS COME".
Text 10: "THANKS BIG BOY".
Texts 11-23: the energy display for energy 0-12, 20 bytes each. Each has 2 lines of 6 characters. "(" and ")" draw the energy units. $82dd writes the column of the fighter into byte 0 and byte 10.
The 13 characters other than A-Z that the text printer draws: 0-9, space, "(" and ")".
Font glyph of each character in text_special_chars.
Column of the energy display of fighter 0 and 1 (0 and 34).
Five score digits (00010) that $83ac adds to the score for each unit of time that remains.
Pointers to the 4 corner animations. $81c1 plays animation n when $5b,x holds $80+n.

Corner animation: column, row, width and height in cells, then frame addresses. A word below 4 is a command. Commands: 0 restarts, 1 jumps to the offset that follows, 2 starts the animation that follows, 3 stops.
Pointers to the pose sequence of each move $00-$1d. The move number is in $67,x (bit 7 set).

Move sequence: pose numbers, then $ff and a command. 0 loops, 1 sets the move to 1, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. Command 3 starts the move that follows (move $9d also turns the fighter). Other commands hold the last pose.
Not in build V 05 05 87: pose $2e before the $ff. That build ends this sequence after pose $2d.
No code and no table starts move $15. Its pose $3e uses the pose record of pose $0d.
Moves of fighter 1 ($68) that make $8956 update fighter 0 first. Else it updates fighter 1 first.
Moves that $8626 and $86c5 do not change. $8626 reads no joystick and $86c5 does not start move $1a.
Pointers to the pose records of poses $00-$5a. The pose number is in $6f,x.

Pose record: 9 sprite part numbers (3 x 3 grid), move flags, step size, sprite count. Part n is at $0800+64n, 0 is empty. Move flag bits 3 and 4 move the fighter by the step size. 4 bytes follow for each sprite. Sprite bytes: pointer minus $20, colour (bit 7 set: multicolour, else fighter_colours), Y position, X offset.
The 12 poses that can hit. $8838 finds the pose of the attacker here. Entry n selects hit list n.
Pointers to the hit list of each attack pose.
Hit list: pairs of defender pose and hit record number. $ff ends the list. Build V 05 05 87 has defender pose $5b in lists 0, 1, 3, 5, 8, 9 and 10. This build has $5a.
Hit list 5. Not in build V 05 05 87: poses $0e, $0f, $10 and $19 with record 10. That build has pose $23 with record 12.

Hit records, 4 bytes each (39 records). $8845 reads record n at $c7ed+4n. Byte 0: distance mask (ANDed with bit_masks of the distance). Byte 1: new move of the defender, 0 for none. Byte 2: hit_sounds entry (high nibble), energy loss when not 0 (low nibble). Byte 3: hit_sprite_effects entry (high nibble), score_values entry (low nibble). 0 selects none.

Hit records, 4 bytes each (39 records). $8845 reads record n at $c7ed+4n. Byte 0: distance mask (ANDed with bit_masks of the distance). Only bits 0-3 are set, so only the distances 0-3 give a hit. Byte 1: new move of the defender, 0 for none. Byte 2: hit_sounds entry (high nibble). A low nibble that is not 0 takes 1 energy from the defender. Byte 3: hit_sprite_effects entry (high nibble), score_values entry (low nibble). 0 selects none. No hit list uses records 1, 7 and 9.
Records $11 and $12: the defender starts move $99, with no damage and no points. The hit lists of the attack poses $24-$26 (move $91) use them.
Sound requests for $dd, $de and $df, 3 bytes each (5 entries). A zero byte leaves that request.
Hit sprite effects, 3 bytes each: sprite animation, Y position, X offset. Entry 0 is not used.
Score values, 5 digits each: 0, 500, 200, 100, 50. Entry 0 is not used.
Moves that play a sound at one step of their sequence (7 entries).
Sequence step ($69,x) of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Sound request for $dd and $de of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Colour of the hires fighter sprites for each level in $be (8 entries).
Pointers to the AI column table of each level in $be (8 entries).
AI column tables, 32 bytes each. A random number (0-31) selects a column (0-7) of the AI joystick row.
Distance band (0-7) for each distance between the fighters in $aa (0-39).
Pointers to the AI row of each pose $00-$5a of the other fighter. Entries $1b and $1f point to ai_row_15. Build V 05 05 87 points them to ai_row_02 and ai_row_0b.
AI rows, 8 bytes each: one byte for each distance band. The byte selects an AI joystick row.
Byte 0 selects AI joystick row $16. Build V 05 05 87 has $13.
Row $0a. No entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
No entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
Not in build V 05 05 87: a new AI row. Entries $1b and $1f of ai_row_ptrs point here.
AI joystick rows, 8 bytes each (23 rows). $86fd reads row n at $cb81+8n. Each byte is a joystick value: bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, bit 4 fire.
Row 8. It has the same bytes as row 4.
Row 21. Bytes 0, 5 and 6 are $1a. Build V 05 05 87 has $12, $06 and $06.
Not in build V 05 05 87: joystick row 22. Byte 0 of ai_row_01 selects it.
Pointers to the sprite animations $00-$15. The animation number is in $0292,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite animation: frame time, colour and flags, then sprite pointers minus $20. Flag bits: 7 multicolour, 6 wide, 5 tall. $ff and a command end it. 0 loops, 1 stops the sprite, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. 3 starts the animation that follows.
A copy of sprite_anim_04. No pointer points here.
Animations $0b-$0e: the princess (frames $53-$56).
Animations $0f-$14: Drax (frames $57-$5c).
The bolt of Drax (frames $5d-$5f).
Pointers to the 4 sprite set-ups that $8e31 selects with $cb.
Pointers to the 4 figure records of the final stage: Drax stands, Drax throws, the princess, a princess variant. $8e31 selects one with final_scene_pose ($cb).
Sprite set-up, 12 bytes: animations of sprites 3-0, X positions of sprites 3-0, Y positions minus $a2.
Figure record 3. No code writes 3 to final_scene_pose, so nothing uses this record. Only this record has animation $0e (frame $56).
Start motion of the goblin (sprite 4). $84b6 selects one of the 2 entries with bit 0 of the raster line.
Start motion of the bolt of Drax (sprite 4). $84b6 selects one of the 2 entries with bit 0 of the raster line.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each goblin motion. One of these moves of fighter 0 removes the goblin.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each bolt motion. One of these moves of fighter 0 lets the bolt pass.
Pointers to the sprite motions $00-$0b. The motion number is in $025a,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite motion: steps of 4 bytes. Directions (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right), speeds (high nibble X, low nibble Y), frames, command. Commands: 0 next step, 1 new motion and animation follow, 2 new motion follows, 3 step follows, 4 stops. Other values: a sound request follows.
X offset of sprites 0-2 from the fighter for each facing. $910d uses it for move $88.
Animation of sprite 0 for each facing ($910d). The 2 bytes after it are not used.
Animations of sprites 1 and 0 that $96a3 starts.
Animations of sprites 4 and 3 that $9703 starts.
Motion of sprite 0 for each facing ($910d).
Motion of sprite 1 for each facing ($910d).
Motions of sprites 1 and 0 that $96a3 starts.
Motions of sprites 4 and 3 that $9703 starts.
Pointers to the joystick direction list of each facing ($91,x).
9 joystick directions: none, forward, back, down, up, down-forward, up-forward, down-back, up-back. $865f finds the index.
The same list for facing 1: left and right are swapped.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is not pressed.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is pressed.

Move selection rows, 9 bytes each (12 rows): the next move for each direction index of joystick_dirs. $866d reads row n at $ce8b+9n. Row 7, direction 7 (down-back) is 0. Build V 05 05 87 has $92 there.
Bit n for index n (8 bytes): sprite bits, voice bits and distance bits.
All bits except bit n for index n (8 bytes).
Address of each of the 9 sprite parts in the fighter buffer at $05ca. The buffer has 3 x 3 parts, 9 bytes for each line.
Offset in the fighter buffer of each of the 63 bytes of a sprite part.
Offset in the work bitmap of each byte of a fighter buffer line, from the last byte to the first. Each byte fills one cell column.
Offset of character rows 0-7 in the work bitmap (320 bytes each).
Nothing reads these bytes: 14 zero bytes and $ff. $cf80-$cfa1 is not in the program. Build V 05 05 87 has the $00/$ff RAM fill pattern at $cf20-$cfff.
Nothing reads these bytes: 93 zero bytes and $ff at $cfff.
Bitmap of the arena that is not on screen: character rows 7-22, columns 4-35, 256 bytes for each row. $8f63 swaps it with $a69a-$b699 when the arena changes. The code sets $01 to $20 to read it.
Screen RAM of the arena that is not on screen, 40 bytes for each row. $8f8c swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $4400. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e000-$e3ff.
Nothing reads these 24 bytes. They are the same as $47e8-$47ff: $e000-$e3ff started as a copy of all 1 KB of the screen RAM at $4400.
Colour RAM of the arena that is not on screen. $8f8c swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $d800. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e400-$e7ff.

Colour RAM of the arena that is not on screen. $8f8c swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $d800. The hit-record bug at $87e5 reads $e422-$e425 as a hit record. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e400-$e7ff.
Nothing reads these 24 bytes. As in $e400-$e7e7, the low nibbles are colours and the high nibbles vary, as in a read of colour RAM: $e400-$e7ff started as a copy of the colour RAM at $d800.
Font of the text printer, 8 bytes for each glyph (39 glyphs): space, A-Z, 0-9, "(" and ")". $938d gives the glyph address $e800+8n. $92eb makes multicolour cells from each glyph.

Font of the text printer, 8 bytes for each glyph (39 glyphs): space, A-Z, 0-9, "(" and ")". $938d gives the glyph address $e800+8n. $92eb makes multicolour cells from each glyph. The hit-record bug at $87e5 reads $e81a-$e81d, $e822-$e825 and $e82e-$e831 as hit records.
72 zero bytes after the font. Nothing reads them.
8 frames of the corner animations, 4 x 4 cells each (128 bytes), cell by cell and row by row. $e980-$eb7f are the right corner frames, $eb80-$ed7f the left corner frames.
Tune data of tunes $00-$56, in the RAM under the KERNAL ROM. The format is the same as at $a277.
Nothing reads these bytes. They hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
13 sprites. $8df6 swaps them with the sprites at $54c0-$57ff (pointers $53-$5f). $8497 calls it after a won bout at level 7.

13 sprites of the final stage: the princess (pointers $53-$56), Drax ($57-$5c) and the bolt ($5d-$5f). $8df6 swaps them with the sprites at $54c0-$57ff (pointers $53-$5f). $8497 calls it after a won bout at level 7.
Nothing reads $ff80-$fff9. $ff80-$ffcf hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
6502 code that writes the C128 MMU registers $ff00 and $d505, then jumps to $1100. The program does not run it.
$fff0-$fffe hold the same bytes as $9ff0-$9ffe, a part of freq_table.
$fff0-$fffe hold the same bytes as $9ff0-$9ffe, a part of freq_table. $ffff repeats the byte at $fffe.
NMI vector. The start at $8009 writes $952f (an RTI) here.
Reset vector RAM. The program does not use it.
IRQ vector. The start at $8009 writes $94fe (the IRQ handler) here.
